text.p: Clothing retailer Country Road Ltd said on Tuesday Australian trading conditions had been difficult in the second half of the year to June 30, 1996 and sales continued to be difficult in the current 1996/97 year.
"Consistent with reports from other retailers, Australian trading conditions in the second half of the year have been difficult," Country Road said in releasing its 1995/96 results.
"Current sales continue this trend," it said.
Country Road earlier reported its net profit fell 36 percent to A$10.17 million in 1995/96.

There were no abnormal items in the latest year but an abnormal gain of A$5.76 million the previous year meant net profit before abnormals at A$10.17 million was slightly above the A$10.132 million recorded in 1994/95.

Country Road chief executive Mike Howell said the Australian performance had been hurt by a difficult retail market for clothing, "which had placed considerable pressure on sales turnover and margins."
He said, however, that inventories had been carefully managed.
New Zealand continued to provide a strong contribution and had recorded an increase in sales of 11 percent above last year, Howell said.
"Trading (in New Zealand), however, has fallen away in recent months."
Howell said the restructured U.S. operations had considerably improved their performance.
"There are indications of improved trading conditions in the USA," he said.
"This allied with our new partnership with Itochu provides the opportunity for us to capitalise on the base we have established and achieve profitability."
Last week Country Road announced it had agreed to sell 25 pecent of its U.S. operations to Japanese trading house Itochu Corp and that Itochu would market Country Road products in Japan.
Howell said Country Road's Asian business had continued to perform strongly.
"We are looking to further expansion in this market."
Country Road shares closed two cents firmer at A$1.82 on Monday.
